text:
Elias Lindholm scored four goals against Washington last Saturday, and Daily Faceoff asked the question Boston fans have been asking for two years: is he finally living up to his contract? Boston Sports Journal framed it as a healthy Lindholm finally getting rewarded.

So far, yes. He has 11 goals and 22 points in 25 games, and he ranks 10th of 568 skaters in our wins added, with a lot of his goals coming when they mattered. The Bruins get about 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, six points better than without him. That is a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level.

Part of it is real. His own chance creation is up to about 1.0 expected goals per 60, from 0.86, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a signature play: 23% of his setups come across the royal road, triple a typical forward. Part of it isn't: he is shooting 21% against 15% last season, with 11 goals on 7.4 expected. Expect the goals to slow, but the player underneath looks better than the one Boston had last year. He has no points in the two losses since the four-goal night.
